# DKR-030: Projects do not share networks

- **Group:** Docker
- **Severity when it fails:** high
- **Root:** the full result needs `sudo`. Without root this check reports `unknown`, never a pass.

## Why it matters

Containers on one user network reach each other by name on every port. When projects share a network, a compromise of one app reaches the others, and fails when a peer is a database (postgres, mysql, mariadb, mongo, redis, valkey, clickhouse) that usually trusts its network. Projects come from the Coolify project label, the compose project or the swarm stack; plain containers are their own project. The reverse proxy joins every project network by design and is left out; the default bridge is not judged.

## Verify by hand

```sh
docker network ls; docker network inspect <network> --format '{{range .Containers}}{{.Name}} {{end}}'
```

## How to fix it

Give each project its own network and attach the reverse proxy to each one. In Coolify, give each project its own destination or network instead of the default one.

## What a fix can break

Apps that reached another project's service by container name need an explicit, narrow connection (a shared network for just those two, or a published port).

Run `stackward explain DKR-030` for the same text in your terminal. [All checks](index.md).
